text:
oncall-bot: PAGING: High token latency + KV cache growth detected for hosted inference (region-us-west). incident_id=INC-2026-0422. Thresholds breached: token-p95 > 450ms, kv-cache-memory > 85%

sara: I'm on it. seeing a spike in continuous-batching queue depth too. frontend errors ~502 for a subset of customer routes.

miguel: digging into runtime traces now. early observation: speculative-decoder is producing more drafts than targets, causing KV cache entries to inflate. looks like draft/target sync is diverging -> cache duplication.

kevin: moving to split traffic to fallback model-variant to reduce load. can we flip speculative decoding off for this pool as a quick mitigation?

sara: yes. set speculative=false on pool redwood-arm64-usw-2? ops-bot, can you run config toggle?

ops-bot: Running patch: set /pools/redwood-arm64-usw-2/speculative=false -> success. rolling restart batch=3

lia: Customers reporting slow responses: acct:zoomy-inc and acct:playpack. I messaged both with ETA 15m.

miguel: after toggle, queue depth dropped ~40% in first 90s, p95 latency down ~120ms. however kv-cache memory not yet under threshold, we still see many stale entries from duplicated draft keys.

sara: can we trigger controlled eviction of speculative prefixes? any safe eviction script?

kevin: yes — we have a targeted eviction that deletes keys matching "spec-draft:*" with TTL cutoff older than 10m. will run with dry-run first. command: ```python tools/kv_admin.py --pool redwood-arm64-usw-2 --evict-pattern "spec-draft:*" --min-age 600 --dry-run```

miguel: run dry-run, then one shard at a time. if eviction removes >25% of entries on a shard it could temporarily spike load, so pace it.

kevin: dry-run shows ~18% deletable keys on shard-7, ~3-6% others. proceeding with paced eviction.

ops-bot: Eviction job started: job_id=evict-1805123456-01. shards=1..4 paced 30s.

sara: monitoring. kevin/miguel, keep me posted on latency and error rates. lia, update customers in 10.

lia: noted. pinged Zoomy that we're mitigating and will follow up with root cause.

miguel: eviction completed for shards 1-4, memory down 12%. p95 latency continues to improve. starting next batch of shards 5-8.

kevin: shards 5-8 showed a small transient CPU bump on shard-6 during eviction but recovered. total kv-cache mem now 62%.

sara: good. what's the plan to prevent recurrence?

miguel: immediate: add a guard in the speculative-decoder path to dedupe draft keys before writing to KV cache; fallback: cap speculative drafts per request to 2. mid-term: add instrumentation on draft/target ratio and set alert at 0.8->1.2 deviation.

kevin: I'll open a PR for the dedupe guard and the per-request cap. expecting review + deploy to staging in ~4h. PR: https://git.company/pr/infra/1234

lia: ops note: two customers had transient errors for ~6-12 minutes, no data loss. flagged for follow-up by CSMs.

sara: status update for postmortem: impact window 1805123456 -> 1805123620. root cause: speculative-decoder -> draft/target divergence causing KV cache blowup and continuous-batching pressure. mitigations: speculative toggle, paced eviction, traffic split to fallback variant.

miguel: adding metric names and graphs to the incident doc. we should include sample logs. example: ```RUNTIME_WARN spec-sync: draft_count=16 target_count=3 req_id=abc123 pool=redwood-arm64-usw-2```

ops-bot: Canary/rollback hooks: model-variant fallback remains active, speculative toggle set to false. no rollback required.

kevin: PR opened for hotfix config to set speculative=false as a temporary auto-failover when kv-cache > 80% for > 60s. link: https://git.company/pr/infra/1235

lia: customers updated. Zoomy confirmed degraded UX but no billing impact. Playpack wants a postmortem.

sara: I'm going to hand off to allen for night coverage. allen, summary: incident id INC-2026-0422, mitigations done, monitoring in stable state, follow up items: PR reviews, postmortem, customer comms.

allen: taking over. I'll watch for regressions and ensure follow-up tickets created. thanks team. :thumbsup: 

sara: thanks all. moving to incident-closed-warmstate; will draft postmortem tomorrow.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=stabilized -> moving to monitoring. original_thresholds_cleared=true.
